source.label: thm: depends-on-x
source.quote: If the above conditions are satisfied, there exists an allocation rule $\{\phi_\tau\}$ such that \lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}{\mathsf E}_{C_0}\{T_{inf}(t)\} <\infty. Such a rule is obviously uniformly good.

results.notes: Expected inferior sampling time bounded; achieved by Algorithm 2 (proof in Appendix C).

conditions: context set X finite with P_G(X_t=x)>0 for all x
mu_theta(x) strictly increasing in theta for all x

source.label: thm: lbd-X-depends-on-x
source.quote: Under the above assumptions, for any uniformly good rule $\{\phi_\tau\}$, $T_{inf}(t)$ satisfies \lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}{\mathsf P}_{C_0}( T_{inf}(t)\geq\frac{(1-\epsilon)\log t}{K_{C_0}})=1 ... and \liminf_{t\rightarrow\infty}\frac{{\mathsf E}_{C_0}\{T_{inf}(t)\}}{\log t}\geq \frac{1}{K_{C_0}}, where ... K_{C_0}=\inf_{\theta:\theta>\theta_2}\sup_{x\in{\mathbf X}}\{I(\theta_1, \theta|x)\}.

results.notes: Also an in-probability statement: P(T_inf >= (1-eps) log t / K_C0) -> 1. Quantity is expected inferior sampling time.
